In iOS 27, Apple says it has paid special attention to making its software "more responsive, more reliable, and more delightful." This update includes a number of fixes designed to make iPhones run faster, including updates for network handoffs.

iOS 27 makes switching between Wi-Fi and cellular smoother than ever

Apple says that under the broad goal of "platform improvements," they have done extensive work in iOS 27 to make iPhones run faster.

The speed improvements are reflected in many areas, and one of the things Apple particularly highlights is network switching.

In the past, whenever an iPhone switched between Wi-Fi and cellular, there would always be an annoying delay.

When you leave home and walk out of Wi-Fi range, the iPhone still thinks it's connected to Wi-Fi, so it cannot immediately switch to cellular.

The result is that you'll briefly be in a state with no data connection at all.

When this happens, a common workaround is to open Control Center and temporarily turn off Wi-Fi to force the iPhone to switch to cellular immediately.

However, with iOS 27, you should no longer need to do this.

Apple says: "Network handoffs between cellular and Wi-Fi are smoother than ever."

Basically, iOS 27 makes the iPhone smarter about deciding when to switch from Wi-Fi to cellular, and vice versa. After many months of beta testing, Apple appears to have delivered on that promise.

So far, I can hardly recall needing to manually turn off Wi-Fi in iOS 27. Even during network handoffs, my iPhone maintains a stable connection. Hopefully when iOS 27 officially launches, all users will enjoy the same experience.

How has your network switching experience been using iOS 27 beta? Let us know in the comments.
